name: Genetic Superficial Corneal Dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Genetic Superficial Corneal Dystrophy Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of bilateral superficial corneal epithelial opacities visible on slit-lamp examination
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with superficial corneal dystrophies
No evidence of stromal or endothelial corneal involvement on clinical and imaging studies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Bilateral superficial corneal epithelial opacities plus either positive family history or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by family history and genetic testing when available.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic punctate or patchy epithelial lesions visible on slit-lamp exam
searchTerms: cloudy spots on front eye surface both eyes
white patches on cornea of both eyes

pathognomonic.notes: Episodes of epithelial breakdown causing ocular discomfort

common.notes: Light sensitivity often reported by patients

common.symptomName: Foreign body sensation in the eye

common.notes: Transient visual disturbances related to epithelial irregularities
searchTerms: blurred vision that comes and goes

common.notes: Dry eye symptoms secondary to epithelial changes

occasional.notes: Small cystic lesions occasionally seen on confocal microscopy
Localized fibrosis beneath the epithelium in chronic cases

rare.notes: Rare development of new blood vessels in the cornea
Rare infectious complication due to epithelial defects

rare.symptomName: Corneal scarring leading to vision loss
rare.notes: Rare severe complication in advanced disease
searchTerms: eye surface scars leading to poor sight

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing superficial corneal epithelial opacities
Confocal microscopy revealing epithelial microcysts and absence of stromal involvement
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as TGFBI or others associated with superficial corneal dystrophies
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic map-like and fingerprint patterns on corneal epithelium
Presence of subepithelial microcysts and fingerprint lines
Typically sporadic with less clear genetic inheritance
May have recurrent erosions but different epithelial patterns

redFlags: Severe vision loss not explained by superficial lesions
Signs of secondary infection or keratitis
